Log-Survival Derivatives of the Weibull, Mean and Shape

Source: R/weibull3_distrib.R
weibull3_log_surv_derivs.Rd

Computes the derivatives of order o of \(\log S(q) = -e^{h}\), \(h = \sigma\{\log q - \log m + \log\Gamma(1 + 1/\sigma)\}\), in \((m, \sigma)\), as \(-e^{h}\) times the complete Bell polynomial in the partial derivatives of \(h\) (bell_f_ratio()). The function \(h\) is \(\sigma\) times a sum of a function of \(m\) and a function of \(\sigma\), so a mixed partial derivative of \(h\) is nonzero only when it names \(\sigma\) at most once; the pure derivatives in \(\sigma\) are \(\sigma g_k + k g_{k-1}\), where \(g_k\) is the derivative of order \(k\) of \(\log\Gamma(1 + 1/\sigma)\) by the chain rule over the polygamma functions and \(g_0\) is the whole sum. At \(q \le 0\) every derivative is zero.

Usage

weibull3_log_surv_derivs(distrib, q, theta, o)

Arguments

distrib

A Weibull3Distrib object.

q

A numeric vector of quantiles.

theta

A named list with components mean and sigma.

o

The derivative order, 1 to 4.

Value

A named list, one component per multi-index of order o, in the order of hess_names() at order two.

Examples

d <- weibull3_distrib()
distributions7:::weibull3_log_surv_derivs(d, c(18, 480),
                                          list(mean = 60, sigma = 6), 2L)
#> $mean_mean
#> [1] -5.422180e-06 -1.949783e+03
#> 
#> $sigma_sigma
#> [1] -6.987221e-04 -7.100705e+05
#> 
#> $mean_sigma
#> [1] -4.912391e-05  3.720917e+04
#>
